media.title: Hotel Edison, New York — historical view, 1933
media.description: Night view of the Hotel Edison in Midtown Manhattan, photographed shortly after the hotel opened and before Bronisław and Eleonora Kaper stayed there on their arrival in New York in 1934.
media.altText: Black-and-white night view of the illuminated Hotel Edison rising among Midtown Manhattan buildings in 1933.
media.publicCaption: Hotel Edison in Midtown Manhattan, 5 December 1933.
media.publicCreditLine: Samuel H. Gottscho; Gottscho-Schleisner Collection, Library of Congress; Wikimedia Commons, CC0 1.0.
media.rightsNote: Public-domain image. Wikimedia Commons makes this cropped file available under CC0 1.0; the Library of Congress records no known restrictions on publication for the underlying Gottscho-Schleisner Collection negative.

places.publicNote: New York hotel where Kaper and his wife Eleonora stayed on arrival from Le Havre before travelling on to Los Angeles. In his 1975 AFI oral history Kaper recalled the Edison Hotel as the studio's $300-a-week accommodation tier.
